thread.title: Apple Sorry For Slowing Older iPhones, Offers Discount Replacement Batteries

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Sorry For Slowing Older iPhones, Offers Discount Replacement Batteries
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) late Thursday apologized for its handling of a battery management issue that slowed older iPhones. In a message to customers on its website, Apple vowed to be more transparent on such matters in the future and offered a 63% discount on replacement batteries for qualifying handsets.
X Apple refuted claims that it was slowing older iPhones to spur customers to upgrade to newer handsets.
"First and foremost, we have never — and would never — do anything to intentionally shorten the life of any Apple product, or degrade the user experience to drive customer upgrades," the company said. "Our goal has always been to create products that our customers love, and making iPhones last as long as possible is an important part of that."
Apple said it implemented changes to its smartphone battery management about a year ago with the release of a software update called iOS 10.2.1. The software was designed to improve power management during peak workloads to avoid unexpected shutdowns on iPhone 6, iPhone 6 Plus, iPhone 6S, iPhone 6S Plus, and iPhone SE.
"With the update, iOS dynamically manages the maximum performance of some system components when needed to prevent a shutdown," the company said. "While these changes may go unnoticed, in some cases users may experience longer launch times for apps and other reductions in performance."
Apple said it began receiving feedback this fall from some users who were seeing slower performance in certain situations. Apple determined that the chemical aging of batteries in iPhone 6 and 6S series phones was behind much of the degraded experience.
Apple noted that all rechargeable batteries become less effective as they age and their ability to hold a charge diminishes. Device usage also can impact battery performance over its lifespan, it said.
